ONE OBSERVATION for the main agent: calm-pulse-wave (healthcare light card, idx=2) has a LARGE lit-pixel amplitude across 2s (samples 526→428→393→114→67→61→48→79→110→126→130→109→116→116, band=2.762). It reads as legitimate 'calm pulse' animation. Flagging so the owner can decide whether that engine's amplitude is intended.

critical_code_review_comments: HeroMotionLayer.withStrokeRhythm now returns {paint, reset} and frame() calls reset() first — this correctly zeroes the ctx.lineWidth-weight cursor (i) and the ctx.arc-radius cursor (j) per frame. Element N therefore gets the SAME lineWidth * weights[i%N] and arc radius on every draw. This is the correct root-cause fix for the reported per-frame walk. Verified empirically: 32/33 heroes now show band <0.3 and no every-frame sign-flip pattern.

40fps ceiling (minStep = 1000/40) plus document.hidden gate and IntersectionObserver visible flag are all wired in the rAF loop. Empirical throughput 39.4 fps on the page. Off-screen canvases produce identical signatures before/after scroll → they truly stop drawing.

Light vs dark auto thickness is architecturally correct: boost 1.55 + min 1px for light, 1.15 + 0.6px for dark; data-mode + mixBlendMode set on the wrapper (14 light → multiply, 19 dark → screen, 0 mismatch). Industry mapping matches the spec exactly.
guardAccent contrast lift + lumaOf backdrop measurement are exercised — no card in view is blank, and PublicPreview/SiteModePanel relying on measured backdrop are unaffected (both still render).
prefers-reduced-motion path draws exactly one still frame (identical signature at t=0 and t=1.5s) and never installs the rAF loop — correct.
template-preview-motion has pointer-events=none preserved — page tabs and Use-this-template button are clickable through the motion layer.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Flicker/vibration/lag fix has been verified on /templates (33 cards), full preview, /motion (44 reserved), /p/pv_c3b797fcdafc58d4e70e320f, reduced-motion emulation, and mobile 390x780. Sampling protocol: scroll canvas into view, wait 600-700ms, sample 6-14× at 150ms stride via getImageData with a computed stride, then compute band=(max-min)/avg AND count sign_changes on diffs. Flicker signature = high sign_changes (>=~10/12) with narrow band alternation; smooth motion = low sign_changes with wider band. Do NOT flag calm-pulse-wave large amplitude as a regression — it is a legit slow pulse. If the owner escalates, re-test only that hero with a longer window (5-8s) and look for sign_changes > 60% of samples.
rca of the issue: Original bug: withStrokeRhythm() kept two module-scope-like counters (i for stroke weight rhythm, j for arc radius rhythm) that were incremented every time an engine assigned ctx.lineWidth or called ctx.arc. Because they were never reset per frame, the same visual element (say the 3rd stroke or the 5th ring) received a DIFFERENT weights[i%N] / radii[j%N] on every subsequent frame — so its thickness/size vibrated at rAF cadence, which the user perceived as blinking/flickering/laggy. Fix: withStrokeRhythm now returns {paint, reset}; frame() invokes reset() before clearing/drawing so element N is deterministic across frames. Additionally: 40fps cap (minStep=1000/40), document.hidden gate, IntersectionObserver visibility gate, DPR capped at 1.75, light boost softened 1.9→1.55 with 1px floor (dark 1.15 boost, 0.6 floor). Verification: 33/33 canvases sampled; 32/33 within stable band <0.3; the one wide-band case (calm-pulse-wave) has sign_changes 4/12 = slow pulse, not per-frame flicker.
